To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of antibiotics for the treatment of sore throat is not associated with an increased risk of developing acute rheumatic fever, and that the use of penicillin is associated with a lower risk of developing rheumatic fever than the use of other antibiotics.
The use of antibiotics for the primary prevention of rheumatic heart disease in the community is not recommended.

1) antibiotic treatment of acute sore throat in children and adolescents is effective for preventing rheumatic fever; 2) antibiotic treatment is most effective if started within the first 9 days of the onset of sore throat symptoms; 3) the benefit of antibiotic treatment is greatest in children with a history of previous RF, and in those living in endemic areas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new and improved methods for the prevention and treatment of rheumatic fever and rheumatic heart disease in the developing world.
understanding the mechanisms by which bacteria and their products induce the immune response, and the consequences of this response.
understanding how the immune system can be manipulated to prevent and treat autoimmune diseases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an effective, safe, and affordable treatment for rheumatic fever.
the use of antibiotics in the primary prevention of rheumatic heart disease has been successful.
the use of penicillin is the first-line treatment for the prevention of rheumatic heart disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a lot of room for improvement in the way that antibiotics are used, especially for upper respiratory infections and for children.
there are a number of factors that can influence the development of a sore throat, but it is not possible to predict which of these will cause a sore throat.
there is no evidence that the current recommendations for the use of antibiotics in the primary and secondary prevention and treatment of RF are effective.
